claims.claim: DIVIDE returns BLANK for a zero or BLANK denominator unless an alternate result is passed; it outperforms explicit zero checks.
Variables improve performance, reliability, readability and debugging.
Materialised calculated columns can hurt refresh performance because values are derived at refresh time.

concept_html:
In a semantic model, arithmetic belongs in measures. A measure is evaluated at query time, in the filter context of the visual: the slicers, rows and columns that apply to that cell. A calculated column is evaluated row by row when the model refreshes and stored, which costs memory and refresh time and cannot react to slicers.

Three habits make measures correct and readable (Microsoft's DAX guidance, checked September 2026):

  • Use DIVIDE, not /. DIVIDE(numerator, denominator) returns BLANK when the denominator is zero or BLANK, instead of an error or infinity. You can pass an alternate result as a third argument. Microsoft notes it is also faster than testing for zero yourself.
  • Use variables. VAR ... RETURN evaluates an expression once and names it. That improves performance, readability and debugging.
  • Change filter context only with CALCULATE, and say why. CALCULATE([Weighted base], ALL(dim_brand)) removes the brand filter, which is what a share-of-total denominator needs.

A weighted share, the survey version of lesson B8-L1:

Weighted aware % =
VAR aware_w = SUMX ( fact_awareness, fact_awareness[aware] * fact_awareness[weight] )
VAR base_w  = SUM ( fact_awareness[weight] )
RETURN DIVIDE ( aware_w, base_w )

Put the unweighted base next to it as a separate measure, Base (n) = DISTINCTCOUNT(fact_awareness[respondent_key]), so report users see how many respondents stand behind each percentage.

Name measures for what they return, store them in one place (a measures table or the fact table), and set their format strings. A measure that nobody can read is a measure nobody can check.

lines: VAR aware_w = SUMX ( fact_awareness, fact_awareness[aware] * fact_awareness[weight] )
RETURN DIVIDE ( aware_w, base_w )
VAR all_brands = CALCULATE ( [Weighted aware %], ALL ( dim_brand ) )
RETURN DIVIDE ( this_brand, all_brands )

A stored percentage cannot re-aggregate correctly when users filter or group differently.
The base changes with every filter. It must be computed at query time.

recap.back: Measures compute at query time in the visual's filter context. Calculated columns are stored at refresh.
Returns BLANK (or an alternate result) when the denominator is zero or BLANK.
Evaluates once, names parts, improves performance, readability and debugging.
CALCULATE([measure], ALL(dim_brand)): remove only the brand filter.

title: DAX measures that state their filter context
why_html: A report computed awareness as SUM(aware_weight) / SUM(weight) in a measure. In a new market with no fieldwork yet, the base was zero, and the visual showed "Infinity" and "NaN" in cells that the board pack exported to PDF. DIVIDE would have returned BLANK, and the empty cells would have been left empty.
